venue.name: Meyhouse Palo Alto
venue.concept: meyhane (Turkish house of wine/small plates) with a live jazz room

price_level.note: Two different scales; neither is a check average. Recorded as published.

sources.note: address, phone, hours
price level $$$, categories, rating, hours
price band, dining style, dress code, rating, cuisines
Google rating 4.6; listing name 'Meyhouse & Meyhouse Jazz Club'
founders, beverage director, concept
jazz venue opened November 2023

operating_hours._note: Venue's own site and Yelp agree exactly: lunch daily 11:45am-2:00pm; dinner Mon-Thu & Sun 5:00-9:30pm, Fri-Sat 5:00-10:00pm. OpenTable publishes a NARROWER variant (lunch 11:45am-1:45pm; dinner Mon-Thu/Sun 5:00-9:00pm) - that is a last-seating grid, not door hours, and is NOT used here.

_sources.note: hours as published by the venue
conflicting narrower hours - recorded but not used

seating.seats_basis: 'Full Buyout of Meyhouse Palo Alto' is listed with SEATED: 100. This is the seated capacity of a whole-venue buyout, the closest published proxy for the dining-room seat count; it is NOT a table count and may exclude or include bar/patio seats.

rooms.name: Istanbul Room (private dining)
rooms.note: 'provides the perfect ambiance for hosting a party of up to 40 people'; has A/V and a private bar

rooms.name: Meyhouse Jazz room
rooms.note: 'Meyhouse Jazz Palo Alto seats 30 guests per seating'; speakeasy-style, built with SFJAZZ sound engineers

seating.private_events_range: 8 to 100 people (venue site); 10 to 100 people (The Vendry listing)
seating.tables_note: No table count is published anywhere found. Left null rather than inferred from seats.
seating.bar_seats_note: A bar exists and is bookable as a dining area ('Bar seating - 21 and over only'); guests describe 'a large bar'. No seat count published.

sources.note: Full Buyout SEATED: 100; 10-100 private parties
8 to 100 people; Istanbul room up to 40 with private bar and A/V
jazz room seats 30 guests per seating
Dining areas: Main Dining Room, Bar seating - 21 and over only, Outdoor Seating
Outdoor seating attribute and highlight
Max Number of People for an Event: 200

covers_per_service_estimate._status: ESTIMATE - derived, not published. No cover counts are published by the venue.
covers_per_service_estimate._method: 100 seated capacity x assumed turns across the published service window. Turn counts are assumptions, not measurements; the only booking-volume evidence found is OpenTable's 'Booked 33 times today' (parties booked through OpenTable only, one day, excludes phone, walk-ins and other channels).

lunch_daily.rationale: 2h15m window; OpenTable's own FAQ calls lunch the quieter service.

dinner_sun_thu.rationale: 4h30m window (17:00-21:30), includes the 30-seat jazz room's two seatings.

dinner_fri_sat.rationale: 5h window (17:00-22:00); OpenTable FAQ: 'expect a livelier, packed scene on Friday and other weekend evenings'.

peak_windows.label: Dinner prime
peak_windows.evidence: For a 2-top on Fri 2026-09-11 queried on 2026-09-03, OpenTable offered ONLY 6:30, 6:45, 7:00, 7:15 and 7:30 PM - later prime-time slots were not offered, consistent with them already being booked. Jazz first seating's show also begins ~6:30 PM.

peak_windows.label: Jazz second seating
peak_windows.evidence: Jazz site: 'Arrive at 8:00 PM, show begins around 8:30 PM'; sets run ~1 hour 15 minutes.

peak_windows.label: Lunch peak
peak_windows.evidence: Lunch runs 11:45-14:00; multiple reviews describe group/business lunches. Exact intra-service peak is NOT published - the window is inferred from the service length.

service_rhythm.popular_times_note: NOT FOUND. Google Maps served only a signed-out limited view with no Popular Times histogram; Yelp showed no popular-times data.
service_rhythm.turn_time_note: NOT PUBLISHED. The only published dwell structure is the jazz room's two seatings (arrive 17:00 / show ~18:30, and arrive 20:00 / show ~20:30, sets ~75 min), implying roughly a 3-hour first seating for jazz guests. Press describes meyhane guests arriving at 5pm and staying until 11pm. No dining-room turn time is stated anywhere; left null.

sources.note: reservation slot granularity, booked-33-times, dining areas, FAQ on busy nights, noise level
jazz arrival/show times and ~1h15m set length
30 guests per seating
seated capacity 100 used as the estimate base
no popular-times data available signed out

menu._warning: OpenTable also hosts a Meyhouse menu stamped 'Last updated: January 17, 2026' whose prices are LOWER than the venue's own June 2026 menus (e.g. Atom $14 vs $16, Ahtapot $24 vs $25, Levrek $50 vs $55). The OpenTable copy is stale and was NOT used. Every price below is from the venue's own current menu images.

behaviour_notes.note: Meyhane rhythm is long and drink-led, not course-led: guests 'arrive at 5 p.m. to drink and savor small plates, drink some more, eat again, and not leave until 11 p.m.' Model long dwell times and repeated beverage rounds interleaved with food, not a single food push.

Meze come first and arrive in volume, cold before hot: 'our entire tabletop was covered with assorted cold meze', and 'one could easily make a meal out of the assorted hot and cold meze alone.' Expect many low-priced items per check before any main.

Rakı is sold four ways on one menu row - single, double, 1/2 bottle and full bottle - and is 'served straight, in cocktails, or by the bottle for the table to share.' A bottle is a TABLE item, not a per-guest item; a POS must not divide it per cover.
Wine by the glass is sold in two pour sizes on the same line (5oz and 8oz) plus a bottle price, so one wine SKU carries three distinct prices. Sparkling wines are 5oz-only ('NA' in the 8oz column).
A 375ml half-bottle tier exists and is explicitly positioned as 'Perfect for 2 people to share OR Course Pairing' - a distinct SKU size between glass and bottle.
Ordering is family-style and shared by default; guests 'ordered everything family style' and portions are 'generous and shareable'. Item counts per cover will look high and covers-per-item low.

The chef's tasting menu 'Little Little in the Middle' ($105pp) requires the WHOLE table to participate, 2-person minimum - a table-level modifier, not a per-seat choice. The lunch prix fixe carries the same all-or-nothing rule.
Large-format items are priced per table with a per-head extension: Karışık Kebap / Mix Kebap Plater is $260 for 4 people, then $65 per additional guest. A POS must model a base price plus headcount.

Lunch and dinner are DIFFERENT menus with different prices for the same dish name: Lokum is $39 at lunch (6oz) and $65 at dinner (10oz); Pirzola $44 (2 pieces) vs $64 (3 pieces); Alinazik is $49 at both. Flatbreads and pide (Lahmacun $13) are lunch-only.
Late seating is structural on jazz nights: a second seating arrives at 8:00 PM for an ~8:30 PM show, so a 30-cover block lands late and dwells ~75+ minutes past the show start.

Guests dine before OR after the show, and on busy jazz nights indoor tables are unavailable to non-ticket holders - one party 'had to reserve outside because of jazz show inside.' The jazz room removes inventory from the main room.

BYO is real and common: OpenTable lists 'BYO Liquor', 'BYO Wine' and 'Corkage Fee' as features, and buying a bottle off the list waives one corkage. Expect corkage lines on checks alongside wine sales.

The wine list is built around an 'ancient world' thesis - Türkiye, Greece, Georgia, Armenia, Hungary, Lebanon, Israel, Morocco - curated by GM/Beverage Director Refet Tugay, alongside conventional Old/New World sections. Turkish bottles are a deliberate, well-stocked category, not a token.
Bar seating is 21-and-over only, so bar covers cannot include minors - relevant to any seating allocation logic.

Some items are flagged 'limited availability' on the menu itself (Lakerda, Çiroz füme, Sögüş Dil, Blantons, Fortaleza, all ice creams) and Whole Fish of the Day is market price. 86-ing and MP entry are normal operating states here.
Künefe is fired to order: 'Please allow 10-15 minutes for this dessert' - a kitchen-timing modifier that should be carried on the ticket.
Service is noisy and group-heavy at peak; OpenTable rates noise 'Moderate' but multiple reviewers call it loud, and the 20% auto-gratuity triggers at parties of 6+, so large parties are common.
